subject: Which mechanism holds the Source version-freeze approval invariant, measured per layer
method: Each candidate mechanism was removed one at a time; every mutation was confirmed to have changed the file before the suite was run, and the failing case titles were recorded rather than only the counts.
question: When an approved authority version is materially edited so a new version supersedes it, what stops the old version's approval from presenting as current?
answer: The approvals read predicate, in SQL, at read time. Nothing invalidates the stale rows and nothing needs to: they are never selected.

layers.name: read-time SQL predicate
failingCases: scopes both reads by tenant, event and kind, and takes only the unsuperseded version
the version-freeze fence — withdraws an acceptance the superseding edit left behind, and the SQL predicate is what does it
the version-freeze fence — withdraws both Strategy approvals the same way, though nothing in production asks

layers.name: row re-check in the store
layers.mutationEffect: 1 case fails, and only the backstop case
failingCases: the version-freeze fence — fails closed rather than leaking if that predicate is ever widened
layers.note: Redundant while layer 1 holds, and deliberately kept: if the predicate is ever widened the store refuses the whole read rather than handing a stale approval on. Its own case drives it by serving rows that ignore the predicates, which is what a widened predicate looks like from inside the store.

layers.name: contract-side filter
layers.mutation: drop the versionId comparison from the filter
layers.mutationEffect: 2 cases fail, both in source-version-authority.test.ts; 0 cases fail in the suite that executes the store
failingCases: accepts a request only from a named actor approving the exact current version
requires business owner and procurement lead to approve the same strategy version as distinct actors
layers.note: This asymmetry is the defect shape the item names: a guard whose only proof asserts on a pure function's return value can be removed without any test that drives the real read path noticing.

layers.name: planner invalidation list
layers.mutation: give it a consumer that deletes the stale approval rows in the write path
failingCases: the version-freeze fence — does not write to the approvals table when a version supersedes another
layers.note: Run twice: once against the field as it stood, once after removal using plan.supersedesVersionId. Both are decisive. The field is deleted rather than wired, per the item's own acceptance (c).

fixtureFinding.problem: The existing store fixture returns its rows regardless of which predicates the query builder was given.
fixtureFinding.consequence: Deleting the predicate under test leaves every one of its cases green, so a case written against that fixture cannot prove a read-time fence at all.
fixtureFinding.resolution: serveTable applies the recorded .eq/.is predicates to a row set, so the row set is the table and the builder is a query over it. The pre-existing predicate-shape assertion is kept: it says which columns are filtered, which is a different claim from what the filter does.

notFixedHere.measurement: Zero non-test references anywhere in src/ on 1526110e7. The mounted src/app/(maestro)/source/new/[eventId]/page.tsx imports only evaluateRequestVersionApproval and reads only authorityKind: "request".
notFixedHere.andOneThingTheItemDidNotSay: Nothing WRITES the strategy half either. persistSourceAuthorityVersion's only production caller is src/app/api/v1/source/events/route.ts, which persists "request". authorityKind: "strategy" appears in no production path in the repository; every occurrence is in a test.
notFixedHere.whyItIsNotAOneLineWiring: Naming a caller for the resolver is not the cost. The cost is building the Strategy version write path, its payload projection and its approval recording — which is F2's whole exit condition, not a bounded change.
notFixedHere.recommendation: Decide whether F2 is in scope before deciding which of the two resolvers to keep. If it is, the resolver stays and the write path is a separate item. If it is not, delete the resolver with its cases rather than leaving an exported gate nothing calls. Do not resolve it by deleting the resolver as tidy-up: the fence proven here already covers the strategy kind, so the resolver is the only part that would have to be rebuilt.

scope.why: This is the list .github/workflows/unit-suites.yml runs for this directory, so the scope of the measurement is the scope CI will run.
scope.baselineMeasuredIn: a separate detached worktree at origin/main, not a stash of this one
